content.name: Miriam Okonkwo-Schulz
content.title: Staatlich anerkannte Erzieherin, Teaching Assistant and Schulbegleiterin
content.summary: State-recognised Erzieherin with nine years in after-school care, inclusion support and international schools in Frankfurt. Now a teaching assistant in a bilingual primary school, I lead small-group German support and co-planned an inclusion approach that let a pupil with autism move from one-to-one support to full class participation.

experience.title: Erzieherin, Hort (After-School Care)
bullets: Looked after a group of 22 primary pupils aged 6–10 each afternoon, including homework support and holiday programmes.
Introduced a weekly children's council so pupils could vote on activities, which the team kept as a standard practice.
Held 40+ parent conversations a year and wrote development reports for the school.

experience.title: Schulbegleiterin (Inclusion Support Assistant)
bullets: Provided one-to-one school support for pupils with autism and ADHD at two primary schools, funded through integration assistance (Eingliederungshilfe).
Worked with class teachers to structure the day with visual plans and quiet zones, cutting lesson interruptions for my pupil from about 8 a day to 2.
Wrote half-yearly reports for the youth welfare office and joined review meetings with parents and therapists.
Kept learning going in online lessons during school closures by preparing printed weekly plans and daily video calls.

experience.title: Teaching Assistant (Primary)
bullets: Assist in a Year 2 bilingual class of 24, taking small groups for German literacy and maths.
Lead a German-as-a-second-language group for 9 newly arrived pupils; 7 joined regular German lessons within a year.
Co-planned an inclusion approach with the SEN coordinator that moved a pupil with autism from one-to-one support to full class participation over 18 months.
Coordinate the school's afternoon clubs timetable for 120 pupils and 10 club leaders.
